chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He recited: 'that they should lay aside their outer garments', he said: 'the khimar (headscarf) and the jilbab (outer cloak)'. I asked: 'In front of whom?'. He said: 'In front of those who are not displaying adornment'. If she does not do so, it is better for her. And the adornment that they display of it is mentioned in the other verse.

key_terms.الْجِلْبَابَ: The outer cloak or garment covering the body
key_terms.الْخِمَارَ: The headscarf or veil covering the head and neck

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic command to 'lay aside outer garments' specifically refer to according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the command to 'lay aside their outer garments' in Surah An-Nur specifically refers to the khimar and jilbab, indicating a layering system of modesty. He contextualizes this by specifying that this adjustment is permissible in the presence of men who are not 'mutabarrijin' (displaying sexual desire or adornment), thereby linking the physical act of uncovering to the spiritual state of the observer. This interpretation underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the interplay between external dress codes and the internal disposition of modesty in social interactions.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, from Al Halby,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws [24:60] if they put off their clothes. Heasws said: ‘The scarf and the robe’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from af-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

read the words of Allah, . . if they leave aside their garment,’ (24: 60) and said these words refer to veil and gown.’ I then asked, ‘In front of whom can they leave their garments aside?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is in front of those before whom it is not considered a show off with beauty (see [24:31]); but if she did not leave them aside is better and the beautification which is permissible to expose is mentioned in another verse (of the book of Allah).”’ [24:31]
